package_info.why_malicious: No specific malicious software package is described in this report. The report discusses systemic risks in IT infrastructure, focusing on the exploitation of outdated systems and vulnerable open source components. Attackers can leverage unpatched vulnerabilities and lack of supply chain visibility to compromise systems. The report emphasizes the need for robust software supply chain management, vulnerability mitigation, and the importance of maintaining an accurate inventory of software components to prevent exploitation.

behavioral_signatures: Deployment or continued use of outdated or unpatched software components with known vulnerabilities
Lack of inventory or tracking of open source dependencies in production environments
Introduction of software with unmitigated, publicly disclosed vulnerabilities (e.g., unpatched CVEs)
Absence of automated vulnerability scanning or SBOM generation in the software development lifecycle
file_indicators: Missing or incomplete software bill of materials (SBOM) for deployed applications
Presence of legacy or unsupported software versions in production systems
Configuration files referencing outdated or end-of-life dependencies
network_indicators: Unusual outbound connections from critical infrastructure systems following software updates or new component installations
Connections to domains or IP addresses associated with known threat actors after deployment of new or updated software components
Unexpected network activity patterns correlating with the introduction of new open source dependencies
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Implement automated tools to generate and maintain a software bill of materials (SBOM) for all applications. Continuously monitor and scan all software dependencies for known vulnerabilities (e.g., using CVE databases). Flag deployments that include components with unpatched CVEs, unsupported versions, or lack traceable provenance. Monitor for abnormal network activity, especially after software updates or new component installations, to detect potential exploitation of vulnerable components. Establish alerts for the use of legacy or end-of-life software in production environments and enforce policies to prevent their deployment.
